result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.count_selected_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Get count of currently selected edges. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.count_selected_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Get count of currently selected edges. title: >- [Graph.count_selected_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get count of currently selected edges. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get count of currently selected edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24745-L24796){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Count selected edges](/assets/graphs/count-selected-edges.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node grid with edges A–B, B–E, and E–F selected in the accent color. count_selected_edges() returns 3." width="100%"} Returns the number of edges currently in the edge selection. The count is read directly from the selection set in Rust, so it is cheaper than `len(get_selected_edge_ids())` when you only need the size. Use it to check what an edge selection rule matched before acting on it -- for example, to report how many weak ties would be removed by `delete_edges_ws()` -- or to compute simple fractions such as the share of edges above a weight threshold. The selection itself is not changed, and the node selection is not counted. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of selected edges; `0` if nothing is selected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three of these four edges have a weight above `0.5`, so the count is `3`: ::: {#d6c077f6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 0.9), ("B", "C", 0.4), ("C", "D", 0.7), ("D", "A", 0.6)]) .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight > 0.5) ) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A predicate that matches nothing gives `0`. This cycle has no explicit weights, so every edge's `weight` is `None` and no edge passes the guarded test: ::: {#c0641329 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_cycle_graph(n=10) .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight is not None and e.weight > 0.7) ) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0 ``` ::: :::
